prompt:
Reddit post, r/houseplants.
Title: Moonlight Philodendron Diagnoses

I purchased this (I believe) moonlight Philodendron about a month or two ago. I noticed a brown spot upon purchasing but figured it was nothing. Today, I lost a leaf and others are turning brown as well. The plant is still growing new leaves and there are several healthy leaves. My central ac broke in my home so humidity is high and temp has been suitable in here for plant life. I only water when the soil feels dry and not on a scheduled basis. I reported it as soon as I got it.

I did not! I'm still kinda new to this...

What is wrong with my plant?
answer:
**Most likely: bacterial leaf spot**, probably present when you bought it (that first brown spot). The warning signs are the dark, wet-looking greenish-brown blotches with yellow halos, especially on the leaf in your second photo. Warm, humid air from the broken AC and water sitting on leaves help it spread from leaf to leaf. Your watering habit (only when the soil is dry) is good, so keep it up. The healthy new growth is a good sign. Some lower-leaf yellowing after an immediate repot is normal, but these spreading dark patches need action now.

1. **Remove infected leaves today (about 10 minutes).** Wipe scissors with rubbing alcohol. Cut every leaf with dark, wet-looking blotches off at the base of its stem, and wipe the blades again between cuts. Bag the leaves and throw them out rather than composting them.
2. **Keep the leaves dry.** Pour water only onto the soil. If any splashes onto a leaf, blot it dry with a paper towel right away. The leaf in photo 2 still looks wet.
3. **Improve airflow.** Move the plant about 2 feet from other plants. If you have a fan, run it on low nearby a few hours a day so the leaves dry faster.
4. **Check every few days (2 minutes).** Look over the remaining leaves for new dark, wet-looking spots and cut those leaves off the same way.
